channel.title: Bitport Herald
channel.description: Fictional sample stories for offline demos and tests. Not real news: the outlet, the events and the quotes are invented; the places are real so the map can show them.

item.title: Iceland volcano: lava fountains light up the Reykjanes sky
item.description: Lava fountains up to 50 metres high lit up the night sky over the Reykjanes peninsula. Nearby roads were closed as a precaution, officials said. Roads near the eruption site have been closed to sightseers.

item.title: Thousands ride Lisbon's new tram on its first day
item.description: Thousands of people rode Lisbon's new riverside tram on its opening day. The line has 14 stops between the city centre and the river mouth. Queues formed at the first stop before the doors opened.

item.title: Kerala floods: thousands moved to relief camps as heavy rain continues
item.description: Thousands of people have moved to relief camps in Kerala, India, after days of monsoon rain. Rescue teams are using boats to reach flooded villages. Schools in the worst-hit districts will stay closed this week.

item.title: Venice raises its sea barriers in a test before the autumn tides
item.description: Venice has raised its sea barriers for a test ahead of the autumn high tides. Engineers say the 78 gates can hold back a tide of up to 3 metres. The gates lie flat on the seabed until they are needed.

item.title: Coral recovers on parts of the Great Barrier Reef off Queensland
item.description: Scientists say coral cover has grown on parts of the Great Barrier Reef for a second year. “The reef is showing it can bounce back when it gets a break,” a lead researcher said. Researchers warn that another hot summer could undo the gains.

item.title: Morocco desert solar plant reaches full power
item.description: A large solar plant on the edge of the Sahara in Morocco is now running at full power. Its operator says it supplies electricity for more than 1 million people.

item.title: Mexico City closes its historic centre to cars on Sundays
item.description: Mexico City will close the streets of its historic centre to cars every Sunday from next month. The city says walkers and cyclists will get 15 kilometres of open road.

item.title: Norway opens a 27 kilometre road tunnel under a fjord
item.description: A 27 kilometre road tunnel under a fjord has opened on the west coast of Norway. The government says it cuts the journey between two cities by 40 minutes. Until now, drivers had to wait for a ferry to cross.

item.title: Ghana volunteers plant one million mangrove trees
item.description: Volunteers in Ghana have planted one million mangrove seedlings along the coast near Accra. The project aims to protect fishing villages from coastal erosion.

item.title: Bangkok airports handle a record 6 million passengers in a month
item.description: Bangkok's airports handled a record 6 million passengers last month, officials said. Hotels in the city report an occupancy rate of 85 percent. A new terminal opened last year to cope with demand.

item.title: Scotland's first tidal power station starts sending electricity
item.description: A tidal power station off the north coast of Scotland has started sending electricity to the grid. The operator says its 4 turbines can power 7,000 homes. The turbines sit on the seabed where the tide runs fastest.

item.title: Rangers film a rare snow leopard and two cubs in Nepal
item.description: Rangers in Nepal have filmed a rare snow leopard with two cubs in the Himalayas. “It is a very hopeful sign for the species,” a park official said.

item.title: Hurricane Elena cuts power to 1.2 million homes in Yucatán
item.description: Hurricane Elena has cut electricity to about 1.2 million homes on Mexico’s Yucatán peninsula after making landfall overnight. Airports in Cancún and Mérida are closed, the authorities say. Repair crews are waiting for the winds to drop before they can start work.

item.title: Wildfire near Marseille forces thousands to evacuate
item.description: Firefighters are battling a wildfire on a pine ridge north of Marseille. About 3,000 residents have been moved from three villages, local officials say, and a motorway has been closed. Water-bombing planes are flying over the ridge.

item.title: Norway raises interest rates in a surprise move
item.description: Norway’s central bank has unexpectedly raised its main interest rate to 4.75 percent. Most economists had expected no change. Mortgage rates are expected to follow within weeks.

item.title: Court orders Amsterdam airport to cut night flights
item.description: A court in the Netherlands has ordered Amsterdam’s main airport to cut night flights by a third from next year, after a case brought by local residents over noise. The airport says it will appeal.

item.title: Seville records 44 degrees as Spain issues heat alert
item.description: Temperatures reached 44 degrees Celsius in Seville on Wednesday, the highest of the summer. Spain’s weather agency has issued a red alert for the south and asked people to avoid going out in the afternoon. Some schools have moved lessons to the early morning.
